question.text: Under SEBI's scheme categorization/rationalization framework, what is the key rule regarding the number of schemes a fund house can offer per category in the open-ended arena?

answer.text: Only one scheme per category is permitted within a fund house in the open-ended arena
A maximum of three schemes per category is permitted
There is no limit on the number of schemes per category
Only two schemes per category — one for retail and one for institutional investors

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's scheme categorization/rationalization aimed to reduce the number of schemes in the open-ended arena to one per category, mandating that a fund house can have only one scheme per category. This was intended to reduce confusion among investors caused by multiple similarly-positioned schemes from the same fund house. The Trap: The "one for retail, one for institutional" option sounds logical but is incorrect — SEBI's approach was simplification through a strict one-per-category rule rather than differentiation by investor type. Note: The rule applies to open-ended schemes within a single fund house; it standardises how investors and distributors compare categories across AMCs.
